title: What Is Article 226, and When Can You File a Writ Petition?
desc: Article 226 lets the High Court of Uttarakhand at Nainital issue writs against any authority for rights violations or any other legal wrong.
why: People facing an unfair order from a government department, university or local body often ask whether they can go straight to the High Court, and under which law.
keyPoints: Article 226 of the Constitution lets every High Court issue writs against any person or authority in its territory.
It covers both violation of fundamental rights and 'any other purpose', wider than the Supreme Court's Article 32 power.
Five writs are available: habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto and certiorari.
The High Court of Uttarakhand at Nainital can act even if the authority sits outside the state, if part of the cause of action arose here.

p: Article 226 of the Constitution of India gives every High Court the power to issue directions, orders or writs to any person or authority, including the government, within its territory. The High Court of Uttarakhand at Nainital uses this power for violations of fundamental rights and, separately, 'for any other purpose' such as an illegal order by a government department or university. This makes Article 226 wider than Article 32, which only lets the Supreme Court act on fundamental rights.
Article 226(2) adds that the High Court can act even if the authority or government concerned is based outside Uttarakhand, as long as part of the cause of action arose within the state.

sections.h: What are the five types of writs?
p: Habeas corpus orders the release of a person held in illegal detention. Mandamus directs a public authority to perform a duty it is otherwise refusing to do, such as releasing a pending payment or processing an application.

Prohibition stops a lower court or tribunal from exceeding its authority, while certiorari quashes an order already passed without jurisdiction or in violation of natural justice. Quo warranto questions a person's right to hold a public office they were not legally entitled to.

sections.h: When should you approach the High Court directly?
p: Courts usually expect a person to first use any appeal, representation or tribunal remedy already available under the relevant law, before filing a writ petition. A writ petition is normally entertained directly when the order is wholly without jurisdiction, violates natural justice, or no other remedy exists.

whatToDo: Keep a copy of the order or inaction you want to challenge, with the date it was received.
Check whether the law governing your matter provides a departmental appeal or tribunal first.
File the writ petition before the High Court of Uttarakhand at Nainital with supporting documents annexed.
Take legal advice on your own facts before deciding which writ and which forum fits your case.

hi.title: अनुच्छेद 226 क्या है, और रिट याचिका कब दायर करें?
keyPoints: संविधान का अनुच्छेद 226 हर हाईकोर्ट को किसी भी व्यक्ति या प्राधिकरण के विरुद्ध रिट जारी करने की शक्ति देता है।
यह मौलिक अधिकारों के उल्लंघन और 'किसी अन्य उद्देश्य' दोनों पर लागू होता है, जो सुप्रीम कोर्ट के अनुच्छेद 32 से व्यापक है।
पांच प्रकार की रिट होती हैं: हेबियस कॉर्पस, मैंडमस, प्रोहिबिशन, क्वो वारंटो और सर्शियोररी।
नैनीताल स्थित उत्तराखंड हाईकोर्ट तब भी कार्रवाई कर सकता है जब प्राधिकरण राज्य के बाहर हो, बशर्ते वाद-कारण का कुछ भाग यहां उत्पन्न हुआ हो।
